questions.question: What is a habitat, and why are there so many different kinds of living things on Earth?
questions.expected_answer: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives and gets food, water, shelter and space. There are so many kinds of living things because the Earth has many different habitats, and each plant or animal is suited to its own habitat.

questions.question: What does indigenous mean? Name two of South Africa's national symbols and one invasive alien plant.
questions.expected_answer: Indigenous means a plant or animal has always lived naturally in a place and was not brought there by people. National symbols include the springbok, the blue crane, the king protea, the real yellowwood and the galjoen. Invasive alien plants include black wattle, pine and prickly pear.

questions.question: Name three South African habitats and one plant or animal that lives in each.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: fynbos with proteas or the Cape sugarbird; the Karoo with succulents or meerkats; the bushveld with marula trees or elephants; the grassland with blesbok; a wetland with hippos or reeds; the sea with dolphins or kelp.
